findings.location: sections/20-crushed-seed.tex lines 337-339 (fourSenses, Anagogical, first interpretation); web Markdown line 341: 'In the grown tree's branches the one caught up into paradise, and to be caught up into the clouds, rests tuta iam sede, “in a seat now safe” (2 Cor 12:4; 1 Thess 4:16)'
findings.problem: This is carried at the severity iteration 0 gave it. The source is unchanged, and this round re-read it against the tracked Wikisource text of Ambrose, Exp. in Lucam VII.185 ('in cujus frondentibus ramis ... ille raptus in paradisum, in aerem rapiendus et nubes, tuta jam sede requiescat'). The sentence copies the shape of the Latin, and the English does not parse on a first reading. 'The one caught up into paradise, and to be caught up into the clouds' joins a past participle to a bare infinitive with no relative pronoun. The subject is never named, and the body of the study never presents this passage, so a reader meets it here first. The attribution and loci are correct. Under 'Say what the texts say, plainly' this is Latin left for the reader to construe. It occurs once, so it is advisory.
findings.required_result: Name the subject and complete the clause, keeping Ambrose's words and loci. For example: 'Ambrose sets in the grown tree's branches the man who was caught up into paradise and is to be caught up into the air and the clouds (2 Cor 12:4; 1 Thess 4:16), resting tuta iam sede, “in a seat now safe”; the nations gathered from far off fly into them and flourish certae stationis iam securitate, “in the security of a sure station” (VII.185-186).' The rest of the sense is unchanged.

summary: Artifact: the canonical web conversion build/web/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/67-resumed-sixth-after-epiphany.md, SHA-256 293ceca2e890ee0f4714c7943af99fea687f11db59d8d42107fa2e8af9c99410, the hash research/web-artifact.json records and REVIEW_INPUTS seals. The same bytes came from a fresh tools/tpt web-edition conversion into this review's scratch (pandoc 3.11, Markdown 3.10.3), and they are the markdown of the current web-editions browser product (family key 17985301...), which the site renders. Against the iteration-0 seal, the content and evidence identities are unchanged. Only the output and render digests moved (scripts/_workflow.py). REVIEW_SCOPE: web-edition.toml is valid under tools/tpt check-web-edition (1 eligible), records inspected, inspected_by and inspection together, and names these bytes. The install-publication entry in research/production-review.md is accurate: its six accepting-result SHA-256 values and its per-review iteration and severity tallies match the run's results, and its conversion hash and stamp match. Checked: the whole Markdown was read against main.tex and every input. An independent TeX-stripping word comparison (19,085 source words, punctuation attached) found no dropped, added or reordered word. The only additions are the converter's title and subtitle from pdftitle and pdfsubject, the title block, the map-table header, the ten generated chronology rows, the stamp 'Last revised (UTC): 2026-11-11T20:40:01Z' and the rights colophon. Each chronology row matches its annotation payload cell for cell, with ties as no-break spaces. There are 410 italic spans: 399 latin/work/textit macros, the subtitle and the ten Latin blocks. All 49 source labels and the three lane anchors are unique ids. The page has 10 H2 and 46 H3 headings and 24 blockquotes (10 Latin, 14 English, with 14 small-caps labels). Each interpretation is its own H2 and ends in its own Literal, Allegorical, Moral and Anagogical definition list. The map (10 rows), comparison (6 rows) and chronology tables are complete. The ten Latin propers match propers/verified.md. tools/tpt web-edition check --leaf passes: 3 reader outputs convert with every audit. Browser: the page was rendered through the site's own render_source_page, with the real preview admission set, reader contexts and native print pages (928 routes) and no stubs. It was served with QuietServer and driven with ReaderBrowser in headless Chromium at 1280, 768, 390 and 320 px. There is no page-level horizontal overflow. Below the breakpoint the map and comparison tables scroll sideways in their own boxes (content 561 and 737 px), and the date table takes the two-line dossier form. All 67 fragment links resolve, and fragment and contents navigation land headings below the sticky toolbar. Previous (66), Next (f01 Christ the King), Full Study Guide, Synthesis, Homily and Print / Generate PDF are routes of the admitted set. The console is clean, the stamp and colophon show, and there is no model name or TeX debris. Limits: the full public-alpha preview build refused because build/web-figures is not compiled in this checkout, so the page was rendered alone into scratch. Chrome and neighbour pages were checked as routes, not loaded. Generate PDF was not exercised. The synthesis and homily readers were rendered but not reviewed, and all PDFs were outside this review. Patristic quotations were not re-verified beyond the Ambrose locus of WEB-001, which the research and study reviews own. Verdict: PASS. No blocking defect. The standing advisory WEB-001 is carried at its original severity, and the chronology-corpus observation is restated.
